answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on a normalized attestation graph, so influence from trusted anchors decays with path length rather than accumulating through repeated claims. A sybil cluster that behaves like a haven, knoll, or glacier behind a sparse external cut has low conductance: few attestations cross its boundary relative to its volume. Min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit how much anchored walk mass—and, under normalized voting, aggregate weight—can reach that cluster.
